commit_subject: [perps-controller] Make Hyperliquid max withdrawable decimal-safe (#11253)

Apple TV: the UI at tvOS's size. A TV layout is drawn for 960x540, the screen Android TV lays out in; tvOS lays the same screen out in points, 1920x1080, so on an Apple TV everything showed at half size, its type half of tvOS's own. On tvOS the main view is now shown at 2x (a LayoutTransformControl), which keeps one layout for both TVs. Remote Access shows the code and its text together in the screen's middle, the text at most 420 wide, as TV apps show a code; they were at the far left. Checked on the tvOS 27 simulator (the terms, the home, Language, Remote Access) and in CLIENT on an Apple TV 4K.

Apple heads' READMEs: building for an Apple TV - pairing it with Xcode, its tvOS development profiles, a Release device build installed with devicectl, and where the VPN extension's log and memory probe are, with its 50 MB ceiling; CONNECT's is CLIENT's with its own project, its profiles also carrying Sign in with Apple. Replaces the note that tvOS device profiles did not exist yet.

tvOS: the VPN extension gets iOS's memory guards. Its ceiling on an Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, tvOS 27.2) is iOS's, 50 MB, footprint plus os_proc_available_memory (18.1 + 31.6 MB at the extension's start, 26.2 + 23.8 connected), so ConnectorService's connect gate (3) and the QUIC memory watchdog take tvOS in, as the transport and TCP stack options already did.

Kill switch: three levels in one setting (UserSettings.KillSwitch, now KillSwitchMode: Off, UntilDisconnect, Lockdown) in place of the switch and its lockdown option, as a lockdown with the switch off was a state that did nothing. The page shows them as radios (FeaturePageKind.Choice), with the way out as a note under them and a smaller picture above, so the levels start on a phone's first screen; the daemon's command takes the level too ("kill-switch off|until-disconnect|lockdown", its "lockdown" subcommand gone). The tray and the taskbar button show the block while disconnected as a badge of its own, a no-entry sign, with the block's message as the taskbar's text. The words follow (VpnHood.AppUi.Assets.Classic 76940cc). The UI smoke test walks the kill switch's page too, and keeps away from the keyboard: the dev head's "--no-activate" (NoActivateAvaloniaApp) opens its window without activation and under every other window, and hands the foreground back at once when UI Automation's Invoke takes it; the pictures are the window's own drawing (PrintWindow), so the window never comes to the front for them. Tested: KillSwitchTest; the UI walk.
